answer.answer: Formula: for every n>=1, a_n(x)=1+x+...+x^(n-1) in Z[x]. Specialized at x=1: for every n>=1, a_n(1)=1+1+...+1 = n, without dividing by x-1. The proof uses two-step induction: a_1=1, a_2=x+1, and if a_m=s_m and a_{m+1}=s_{m+1}, then a_{m+2}=(x+1)s_{m+1}-x s_m=s_{m+1}+x(s_{m+1}-s_m)=s_{m+1}+x^{m+1}=s_{m+2}.

claims.quote: Formula: for every n>=1, a_n(x)=1+x+...+x^(n-1) in Z[x].
Specialized at x=1: for every n>=1, a_n(1)=1+1+...+1 = n, without dividing by x-1.

derivation_steps.statement: Define s_n(x)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1} x^k in Z[x], so s_0(x)=0 and s_1(x)=1.
Base case n=2: using the recurrence with n=0, a_2(x)=(x+1)a_1(x)-x a_0(x)=(x+1)*1-x*0=x+1=s_2(x).
Induction hypothesis: for some m>=1, a_m(x)=s_m(x) and a_{m+1}(x)=s_{m+1}(x).
For these m, s_{m+1}(x)-s_m(x)=x^m in Z[x].
By two-step induction starting from n=1 and n=2, for every n>=1, a_n(x)=s_n(x)=1+x+...+x^{n-1} in Z[x].
Specialize by the ring homomorphism Z[x]->Z, f|->f(1). The identity gives a_n(1)=s_n(1)=1+...+1 (n summands)=n for every n>=1.
This specialization uses evaluation at x=1, not division by x-1.
